title: C6H6 next-hour prediction - Italy (UCI Air Quality)
summary: We predicted C6H6 one hour ahead using the Italy (UCI Air Quality) data. Random Forest did best on the validation period, so we used it. On the test period (16 Jan 2005 to 4 Apr 2005) its average error was 1.716 µg/m³. Just repeating the last hour's value gave 2.291 µg/m³, so the model was 25.1% better. 33 episodes were flagged: 33 look like unusual pollution and 0 look like data problems.
how_it_was_made: Read the hourly data and treated empty cells and -200 as missing.

Built the inputs: hour, weekday, the reading 1 hour before, the reading 2 hours before, the reading 3 hours before, the reading at the same time the day before, temperature, relative humidity, absolute humidity.
Split the timeline in order: first 60% to train, next 20% to choose the model, last 20% to test.
Tried Linear Regression, Random Forest and XGBoost. Each predicts how much the level changes in the next hour.
Flagged test hours where the miss was more than 7.36 µg/m³ (bigger than 95% of the misses on the validation period).
Grouped flagged hours that were less than 3 hours apart and checked each group for missing data.
